clue.text: Conspicuous military decorations possibly getting you singing

blocks.note: the military business is war, and the word swaps straight in
bling is showy ornament worn to be noticed, and medals are one kind of decoration
'Conspicuous' is what turns plain decorations into the flashy sort; it hands over no letters of its own

explanation.walkthrough: Medals as war bling is the joke the whole surface is built on, and the definition is the single word left at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: singing -> WARBLING: warbling is singing with a trill or quaver in it, the way a bird or a wobbly tenor does.

clue.text: A kick, after millions invested, to have a successful place

indicators.note: money invested is money put into something, and this letter goes in the same way — inside the word, not in front of it

blocks.note: a boot is a kick
M is the standard short form for millions
to have something is to own it

explanation.walkthrough: The surface is football finance — a kick, millions invested. Read again as instructions, 'invested' is the word doing the work.
explanation.definitionFit: successful place -> BOOM TOWN: a town swelling on sudden prosperity, where boom is the surge in trade rather than a noise.

clue.text: Dates ruined by variable boyfriend?

indicators.note: something ruined has lost the shape it was built in, and letters treated that way keep none of their order

blocks.note: five of the six letters, waiting to be rearranged
algebra's variables are x, y and z, and Y is the one wanted here

explanation.walkthrough: 'Dates' looks like the romance the clue is about and is the fodder instead; the romance sits in the definition at the far end.
explanation.definitionFit: boyfriend -> STEADY: your steady is the person you go out with regularly, a noun that survives mostly in the phrase going steady.

clue.text: Opening verse put at the front by Roman poet

indicators.note: it says where the letter lands: at the head of the assembly, ahead of everything the poet has left

blocks.note: V is the standard short form for verse
Ovid is the Roman poet, and this is what remains once his V has gone to the front

explanation.walkthrough: The poet lends his own V to the head of his name. 'Opening' reads as an adjective describing the verse and is the noun definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Opening -> VOID: a void is an empty space, the gap left where something ought to be, which is what an opening is.

clue.text: Worship of sacred figures, i.e. holy art, possibly about right

indicators.note: 'possibly' says these letters could come out as something quite different, which is licence to reorder them
'about' brings the extra letter in among the rest rather than leaving it parked at either end

blocks.note: nine letters of fodder, with i.e. quietly giving up two of them
R is the standard short form for right

explanation.walkthrough: The Greek roots are the way in: hiero- for holy things, -latry for worship, as in idolatry. The clue hands you 'holy art' as the hint.
explanation.definitionFit: Worship of sacred figures -> HIEROLATRY: from Greek hieros, sacred, and -latry, worship — the reverence paid to saints and icons.

clue.text: Small bag fed to horse results in heavy defeat

indicators.note: what is fed to an animal ends up inside it, so these letters are swallowed by the ones naming the horse

blocks.note: a mare is a horse, the female one
S is the standard short form for small, as on a clothing label
a sac is a bag, the anatomical sort

explanation.walkthrough: The surface is a stable at feeding time and the answer is a scoreline; the two pictures share not one word of vocabulary.
explanation.definitionFit: heavy defeat -> MASSACRE: sport borrows the slaughter word for a hopelessly one-sided result, a thrashing rather than a battle.

clue.text: Facing blow at university, succeed, getting degree

blocks.note: a student in residence at Oxford or Cambridge is said to be up
to succeed in a contest is to win it
a degree is D in the crossword's shorthand

explanation.walkthrough: 'Blow' looks like a synonym waiting to be converted and is half the definition instead: to face the blow is to face the wind.
explanation.definitionFit: Facing blow -> UPWIND: a boat sailing upwind heads straight into the wind, so the word means turned towards the blowing air.

clue.text: A system of divination disposing of one longing

indicators.note: to dispose of a thing is to get rid of it, so whatever is named next is thrown out of the letters before it

blocks.note: the clue's own A opens the assembly
the I Ching is the Chinese book consulted for divination, arriving here short of its first letter
one is the letter I, and it is the piece thrown away

explanation.walkthrough: A genuine system of divination is named and then quietly docked. 'One' as I is worth keeping — Roman numeral and pronoun at once.
explanation.definitionFit: longing -> ACHING: an aching for something is a longing for it, physical pain lent to desire in the way English so often does.

clue.text: Defensive position adopted by excellent core of motorists with stronger reason

indicators.note: a child adopted by a family is taken into it, so the defensive position moves inside the word that adopts it
the core of a thing is its centre, so only the letters at the middle of that word are taken

blocks.note: A1 means first-rate, and the 1 is written as the letter beside it on the page
a fort is a defensive position
the three letters at the dead centre of that nine-letter word

explanation.walkthrough: The surface is all traffic and defensive driving, and the answer is a Latin tag from formal argument. 'Excellent' as A1 is a standing crossword trick.
explanation.definitionFit: with stronger reason -> A FORTIORI: the Latin tag used in argument to say a conclusion follows even more surely than the one just granted.

clue.text: A reduced flavouring in jelly

indicators.note: to reduce a thing is to make it smaller, so the word behind it is written short of its final letter

blocks.note: the clue's own A leads the assembly
spice is the flavouring, docked of its last letter

explanation.walkthrough: 'Reduced' is a cooking word in the surface, where a sauce is boiled down, and a shortening instruction in the parse.
explanation.definitionFit: jelly -> ASPIC: the savoury meat jelly that cold dishes are set in, not the sweet pudding the word first suggests.

clue.text: Assail directors about quantity of computer data

indicators.note: what goes about a thing wraps round the outside of it, so the directors' word splits and takes the rest inside

blocks.note: the board is a company's directors, sitting as one body
MB is a megabyte

explanation.walkthrough: A boardroom and a hard drive make the surface, and the answer is artillery. Two very ordinary words hide a bombardment between them.
explanation.definitionFit: Assail -> BOMBARD: to bombard is to attack with a barrage, assailing in the sustained from-all-sides sense rather than with one blow.

clue.text: Special bit of naughtiness concealed by French king’s composer

indicators.note: a thing concealed by something is hidden within it, so these letters are buried between the king's

blocks.note: roi is French for king
S is the standard short form for special
a sin is naughtiness at its plainest

explanation.walkthrough: 'Bit of' looks like an instruction to take a single letter; here it only means a small helping of naughtiness. The king is French and the composer Italian.
explanation.definitionFit: composer -> ROSSINI: Gioachino Rossini, who wrote The Barber of Seville — the general word standing in for one particular Italian.

clue.text: Shade of gold in plant that’s generally green or off-white

indicators.note: one thing in another is buried between its letters rather than written alongside them

blocks.clueFragment: plant that’s generally green or off-white
blocks.note: ivy is the evergreen climber, and the variegated kind is cream where it is not green
or is gold in heraldry, and the crossword's usual way of saying it

explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the very first word, which is where a solver rarely looks for one this bare. OR for gold is worth learning once and owning forever.
explanation.definitionFit: Shade -> IVORY: a shade is a particular tint, and this one is the creamy near-white of an elephant's tusk.

clue.text: Contributor to law enforcement chilled during game? Good

indicators.note: something happening during a match falls inside it, so these letters land between the ones naming the game

blocks.note: polo is the game, one example of many, which is what the question mark admits
a chilled drink is an iced one
G is the standard short form for good

explanation.walkthrough: The surface is a text message — chilled during the game, good — and every word of it is machinery. The definition is the long phrase at the front.
explanation.definitionFit: Contributor to law enforcement -> POLICE DOG: the handler's animal is a working member of the force, finding what officers on their own cannot.

clue.text: City with Grub Street set up in central part

indicators.note: in a down clue, letters set up are read from the bottom of the grid upwards, so they arrive the other way round
what goes in something sits between its letters instead of before or after it

blocks.note: the pith is the central part of a stem or a piece of fruit
Grub Street was the London street of hack writers, ST is street as always, and the six letters go in bottom to top

explanation.walkthrough: The trap is reading 'central part' as an instruction to take a word's middle letters. It is a synonym, and it is the piece everything else goes inside.
explanation.definitionFit: City -> PITTSBURGH: the Pennsylvania steel city, one particular place standing in for the general word.

clue.text: Merry widow and gent, eh? Hint for a film

indicators.note: merry means tipsy, and nobody tipsy keeps things standing in the order they were handed over

blocks.note: fifteen letters of fodder out of four words, with 'and' only joining them up

explanation.walkthrough: 'Hint for a film' reads as the setter offering help, and 'Hint' is four of the fifteen letters. The Merry Widow is an operetta, which is the picture doing the hiding.
explanation.definitionFit: a film -> GONE WITH THE WIND: the definition names only the category, and the 1939 Civil War epic is the title the letters land on.

clue.text: Melted the Ring in a little bit, having a high temperature

indicators.note: metal that has melted has run out of the shape it was cast in, and letters treated so hold none of their order

blocks.note: a whit is the smallest amount there is, as in 'not a whit'
the word 'the' plus the round O a ring draws, four letters run together and melted

explanation.walkthrough: A ring written as O is one of the conventions worth owning early. The enumeration (5-3) is the tell that this is a hyphenated pair, not one long word.
explanation.definitionFit: having a high temperature -> WHITE-HOT: metal heated past red glows white, so the phrase names the top of the visible heat scale.

clue.text: Believes Italy has silver in pits

indicators.note: silver put in the pits goes among their letters, splitting them, rather than standing beside them

blocks.note: I is Italy, the letter on the car plates
mines are pits, the coal sort
AG is the chemist's symbol for silver, from the Latin argentum

explanation.walkthrough: Mining country makes the surface, with Italian silver ore for colour. The definition is the first word, in the sense of supposing rather than of faith.
explanation.definitionFit: Believes -> IMAGINES: in the supposing sense — 'I imagine so' is 'I believe so', a view held without proof rather than a fantasy.

clue.text: Populist speechifying you’d once picked up around giant figure

indicators.note: in a down clue what is picked up is read from the bottom of the grid upwards, so those letters arrive back to front
what goes around a thing sits on both sides of it, split by whatever it surrounds

blocks.note: ye is the old word for you, so ye'd is how you would once have said it
Gog and Magog are the legendary giants whose statues stand in London's Guildhall

explanation.walkthrough: 'Once' is the standard signal for an archaic form, not for a story that happened long ago — that is the reading the surface wants you to take.
explanation.definitionFit: Populist speechifying -> DEMAGOGY: the demagogue's trade, winning a crowd by playing on its fears and prejudices rather than by argument.

clue.text: A new racket followed by broadcaster, getting behind king’s painter

indicators.note: what is followed by something has that thing written straight after it, so the pieces sit end to end
to get behind someone is to stand at their back, so everything assembled so far lands after the king's letter

blocks.note: K is the standard short form for king, as in chess notation
the clue's own A, taken at face value
N is the standard short form for new
a din is a racket, the noisy sense of the word
Sky is the British satellite broadcaster

explanation.walkthrough: 'Racket' is placed to look like tennis and means noise, which is the pivot the whole clue turns on. Everything named goes behind the king rather than in front.
explanation.definitionFit: painter -> KANDINSKY: Wassily Kandinsky, the Russian pioneer of abstract art, one artist standing in for the general word.

clue.text: 1,000 determine to avoid initial riot control area

indicators.note: to avoid a thing is to keep clear of it, and the initial is the letter a word starts with, so the verb comes without its first

blocks.note: K is a thousand, as in a 10K run or a salary
to settle a question is to determine it, and that verb arrives here shorn of its opening letter
the letter avoided: the S that the verb for determine begins with

explanation.walkthrough: The surface is already a police briefing, which is exactly what the definition is about — so nothing in it flags 'determine' as a synonym to be trimmed.
explanation.definitionFit: riot control area -> KETTLE: British police kettle a crowd, penning demonstrators into a sealed stretch of street until they give up.

clue.text: Vineyard owner’s negative comment for some, about half-bottle

indicators.note: what goes about a thing wraps round the outside of it, so the comment splits and takes the rest inside
half of a six-letter word is three letters, and it is the front three that stay

blocks.note: nah is the casual spelling of no that some speakers favour
the first three letters of the six that spell the bottle

explanation.walkthrough: A half-bottle is a real thing on a wine list, which is what makes the instruction invisible in a clue about a vineyard.
explanation.definitionFit: Vineyard owner -> NABOTH: the man in 1 Kings whose vineyard King Ahab coveted and had him killed for, a name doing duty as a description.

clue.text: Charles, heading for Moon and space

indicators.note: the heading of a word is the letter at its head, so only the first one comes across

blocks.note: Chas is the familiar shortening of that name
the letter the Moon starts with

explanation.walkthrough: The surface sends a man to the Moon and the answer is the gap he would be crossing. Crosswords clip first names freely, so Chas is worth expecting.
explanation.definitionFit: space -> CHASM: a chasm is a space in the sense of a gap, a deep split in rock or in an argument, not room to move about in.

clue.text: Crow initially flying, doing this?

indicators.note: 'initially' asks for the letter a word begins with and nothing else of it

blocks.note: the first letter of the bird's name
a bird awing is on the wing, up in the air

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark is the clue pointing back at itself: read straight, the whole sentence describes the noise, and read as instructions it spells it.
explanation.definitionFit: The whole clue reads straight as a description of a crow up in the air giving its harsh call, which is what 'this' points at.

clue.text: Cross about having skill to produce picture?

indicators.note: what goes about a thing sits round the outside of it, so the cross splits and the rest lands between

blocks.note: the tau cross is the T-shaped one, named for the Greek letter
someone having skill is able

explanation.walkthrough: 'Cross' opens the clue looking like an angry setter about to shuffle some letters. It is a noun, and one of the crossword's regular crosses.
explanation.definitionFit: picture -> TABLEAU: a tableau is a scene held motionless by live figures, and by extension any striking grouped picture.

clue.text: Rear of shabby window-shade showing a big gap

indicators.note: the rear is the back end, so only the final letter of the word behind it is used

blocks.note: the last letter of that six-letter adjective
an awning is the canvas shade hung over a window

explanation.walkthrough: The surface hangs a blind at a shabby window and nothing in it suggests sleep or a gap. An instruction sitting at the very start of a clue is easy to read as scenery.
explanation.definitionFit: showing a big gap -> YAWNING: a yawning hole gapes wide open, the sleepy mouth's word transferred to any wide opening.

clue.text: Thing without tail, unknown climbing mountain creature

indicators.note: the tail of a word is its last letter, and 'without' leaves it off
in a down clue letters that climb are written from the bottom of the grid upwards, so they read the other way round

blocks.note: an item is a thing, and here it loses its last letter
an unknown quantity in algebra is x, y or z

explanation.walkthrough: The surface is a tale about some tailless animal, which is the wrong animal entirely. Y for an unknown comes from algebra and turns up constantly.
explanation.definitionFit: mountain creature -> YETI: the abominable snowman said to haunt the Himalayas, known to the world only from the mountains it supposedly walks.

clue.text: Sack that ultimately contains bricks? On the contrary

indicators.note: 'ultimately' points at the end of a word, the letter that comes last of all
'contains' would put the word in front of it round the outside of what follows
it reverses the sentence just read, so the two pieces swap roles and the bricks do the holding

blocks.note: the plastic bricks children build with
the last letter of the word 'that'

explanation.walkthrough: A brand name doing duty as ordinary bricks, and a setter admitting in three words that he has just described the containment the wrong way round.
explanation.definitionFit: Sack -> LET GO: to let an employee go is the polite phrase for dismissing them, which is exactly what sacking is.

clue.text: Pressman, instinctive, with book probing Green manoeuvring

indicators.note: something probing pushes into what it examines, so this letter ends up inside the letters it is named next to
troops manoeuvring shift about into new positions, and letters told to do it keep none of their order

blocks.note: an instinctive reaction is a gut one
the same five letters in a new order, opening up to take another
B is the standard short form for book

explanation.walkthrough: 'Pressman' reads as a reporter and the answer is the man who built the press itself, which is why the definition sits there unremarked.
explanation.definitionFit: Pressman -> GUTENBERG: Johannes Gutenberg built Europe's first printing press, so the word is journalist on the surface and printer in fact.
